question.prompt: A pool contains \(200\text{ m}^3\) of water and drains at \(20\text{ m}^3\) per hour. After draining for \(t\) hours, the remaining water volume is \(V=200-20t\). In this situation, what is the greatest value \(t\) can take?

solutions.explanation: The water volume cannot be negative, so \(200-20t\geq0\), giving \(t\leq10\). Thus, the greatest value of \(t\) is \(10\).
solutions.title: Require a nonnegative remaining volume
